info.title: One Money Mail Mobile API
info.description:
HTTP API (REST-like) for One Money Mail mobile devices. API is based on JSON API standard (http://jsonapi.org/).
## Convention in this docs worth explanation ### 'data' null vs 404 error
__This is related to paths with GET.__ In case request for resource that does not exists, but resource id was passed  for example /customers/123, there will be response with key 'data' set to null.
In case the primary part of resource URL is wrong, for example /custmerz/123, instead /customers/123, there will 404 (not found) error.
## Getting started To access this API, public/private key pair is needed. Please use POST /devices/authKeys to acquire it.
For this request ("/devices/authKeys") only "Date" or "X-Date" http header is required.
Date must be in format 'D, d M Y H:i:s T', in GMT timezone for example ```Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT```
## API request signing Every HTTP request to API must be signed.
[HTTP signatures algorithm](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-cavage-http-signatures-03)
implementation of PHP package [99designs/http-signatures-php](https://github.com/99designs/http-signatures-php) on API side is used for request signing and verifying. The following headers are needed for sign every HTTP request (except the one for key pair acquire): ### X-Request X-Request is SHA1 hash computed from concatenation HTTP method (lower case), ' ', path, ' ', request body. Path is URI part without query.
#### Example 1 We have POST request for the following URL: ``` /v1/devices/authKeys?foo=bar ``` with body: ```
  {
    "data": {
      "type": "devices",
      "attributes": {
        "deviceId": "5c5be929-43ea-4d7d-836f-901f7a7f6d34"
      }
    }
  }
```
so SHA1 will be computed this way, where "." is used for string concatenation: ```
  SHA1 (
    'post' .
    ' ' .
    '/v1/devices/authKeys',
    ' ' .
    '{
      "data": {
        "type": "devices",
        "attributes": {
          "deviceId": "5c5be929-43ea-4d7d-836f-901f7a7f6d34"
        }
      }
    }'
  )
```
#### Example 2 We have GET request for the following URL: ``` /v1/currencies ``` so SHA1 will be computed this way: ```
  SHA1 (
    'get' .
    ' ' .
    '/v1/currencies' .
    ' ' .
    ''
  )
```
### Date or X-Date Date must be in format 'D, d M Y H:i:s T', in GMT timezone. For example: ```Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT```
### Signature This header is mandatory. The value of this header is HTTP signatures algorithm output. Contents of this signature are the following elements imploded with ",": * `keyId=”%s”`, where %s is public key; * `algorithm=”%s”`, where %s is the name of signing algorithm - hmac-sha256 at the moment * `headers=”%s”`, where %s, is the list of http headers names (lowercase) required for sign (x-request, date or x-date) imploded with „ „ * `signature=”%s”`, where %s is „Signature” string encoded with base64 algorithm. "Signature" is "SigningString" encoded with signing algorithm (hmac-sha256)using private key.
"SigningString" is string imploded with new line character (\n) of strings with the following template "%s: %s", where first "%s" is http header name (lowercase) required for signing (x-request, date or x-date) and second "%s" is http header value. Example of full "Signature" header value:
```
  keyId="raph",algorithm="hmac-sha256",headers="x-request date",signature="02x/Q8hZCW07EEukX8s5FogFZ/Q2ggnAayEw9YqRI9I="
```
### Authorization Value of "Signature" http header prefixed with "Signature ", for example
```
  Signature keyId="raph",algorithm="hmac-sha256",headers="x-request date",signature="02x/Q8hZCW07EEukX8s5FogFZ/Q2ggnAayEw9YqRI9I="
```
## Request authorisation - OAuth2 [Password Grant] [Refresh Token Grant] For requests where customer "session" is required, request should be signed ("Signature" header still remains - these are totally independent) with "Authorization" OAuth2 header, for example: ```
  Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImp0aSI6IjFkZjU5ZjQ5NzA2NjA0ZTUzN2I2NzRiM2JiZjdkNWRkNDUwMmFkZmZmNTI0MTY0M2Q3MzAzZDQ3MzlmMmM4YjlkN2EwZTQ2YWI3MDliMWY4In0.eyJhdWQiOiJtb2JpbGVfYXBpIiwianRpIjoiMWRmNTlmNDk3MDY2MDRlNTM3YjY3NGIzYmJmN2Q1ZGQ0NTAyYWRmZmY1MjQxNjQzZDczMDNkNDczOWYyYzhiOWQ3YTBlNDZhYjcwOWIxZjgiLCJpYXQiOjE0OTY3NDkwNDcsIm5iZiI6MTQ5Njc0OTA0NywiZXhwIjoxNDk2NzQ5OTQ3LCJzdWIiOiIyOTI4NjEiLCJzY29wZXMiOlsibW9iaWxlX2FwaSJdfQ.r2l-8nH2jin81HwtL-nZautTjupOphJV2qMWmlH-NEHRtMst9AAV5SjbvyAa0os-HBcrFYNHZ-bg498WswcqJmo3wQEo--NqdOHMDvqpBY_Gd2jE8sWZrgwVFoG5zBDhTO55cIsJH85MEHQnp_WDre-7OHaFKOYeICnbjlpdy0DLr2WSiLOxc3va56TDeqW2fDFcXaroN6uetWW2TlwxAaEVBmKplocqH7v_PAb-AQ2UGTD_TnyR3Rpre6zlvlyfldqwaz3mPrw485YfBhb9RLlVH-SSg0k2S8rBQ8cQWomYdrdAv1fhh-1fay6aKPFt4fQZn5azui5gzKT433WOkg
```
### OAuth2 - tokens acquire To acquire OAuth2 tokens please proceed to: ``` /customers/login ```
To refresh session token using refresh token, please proceed to: ``` /customers/refreshToken ```
## Request authorisation for machine2machine - OAuth2 [Client Credentials Grant]
For all requests from external application should be signed (“Signature” header still remains - these are totally independent) with “Authorization” OAuth2 header. Endpoint accesses with this grant is limited, is only use for machine to machine connections
Header example: ```
  Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImp0aSI6IjFkZjU5ZjQ5NzA2NjA0ZTUzN2I2NzRiM2JiZjdkNWRkNDUwMmFkZmZmNTI0MTY0M2Q3MzAzZDQ3MzlmMmM4YjlkN2EwZTQ2YWI3MDliMWY4In0.eyJhdWQiOiJtb2JpbGVfYXBpIiwianRpIjoiMWRmNTlmNDk3MDY2MDRlNTM3YjY3NGIzYmJmN2Q1ZGQ0NTAyYWRmZmY1MjQxNjQzZDczMDNkNDczOWYyYzhiOWQ3YTBlNDZhYjcwOWIxZjgiLCJpYXQiOjE0OTY3NDkwNDcsIm5iZiI6MTQ5Njc0OTA0NywiZXhwIjoxNDk2NzQ5OTQ3LCJzdWIiOiIyOTI4NjEiLCJzY29wZXMiOlsibW9iaWxlX2FwaSJdfQ.r2l-8nH2jin81HwtL-nZautTjupOphJV2qMWmlH-NEHRtMst9AAV5SjbvyAa0os-HBcrFYNHZ-bg498WswcqJmo3wQEo--NqdOHMDvqpBY_Gd2jE8sWZrgwVFoG5zBDhTO55cIsJH85MEHQnp_WDre-7OHaFKOYeICnbjlpdy0DLr2WSiLOxc3va56TDeqW2fDFcXaroN6uetWW2TlwxAaEVBmKplocqH7v_PAb-AQ2UGTD_TnyR3Rpre6zlvlyfldqwaz3mPrw485YfBhb9RLlVH-SSg0k2S8rBQ8cQWomYdrdAv1fhh-1fay6aKPFt4fQZn5azui5gzKT433WOkg

post.summary: Third registration step - new / offline clients
post.description: If all data is correct, creates customer account and sends activation email. Then use customers/accountActivation to activate it with token from email. In case that customer already have an account in system that was created by one of the agents, send an verification token to the client via SMS. This token should be then passed to `customers/registrationStepThird` `PATCH` endpoint, and - if it's correct - an activation email will be sent. Then proceed email token with `customers/accountActivation`.
